summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems must establish and document a proportionate post-market monitoring system for the nature and risks of the system.
quote: "Providers shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system in a manner that is proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks of the high-risk AI system."
legal_practice_note: A legal-AI vendor whose system is high-risk must operate documented post-market monitoring.

summary: The post-market monitoring system must actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant performance data throughout the high-risk AI system lifetime.
quote: "The post-market monitoring system shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data which may be provided by deployers or which may be collected through other sources"
legal_practice_note: High-risk legal-AI providers must analyse deployer and other data to check continuing compliance.

summary: Post-market monitoring must allow the provider to evaluate continuous compliance with Chapter III Section 2 requirements and, where relevant, interactions with other AI systems.
quote: "allow the provider to evaluate the continuous compliance of AI systems with the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2. Where relevant, post-market monitoring shall include an analysis of the interaction with other AI systems."
legal_practice_note: Compliance monitoring for high-risk legal AI must consider continuing conformity and relevant interactions with other systems.

summary: The post-market monitoring data obligation excludes sensitive operational data of deployers that are law-enforcement authorities.
quote: "This obligation shall not cover sensitive operational data of deployers which are law-enforcement authorities."
legal_practice_note: This carve-out is specific to law-enforcement deployers rather than ordinary legal practice.

summary: The post-market monitoring system must be based on a plan that forms part of the Annex IV technical documentation.
quote: "The post-market monitoring system shall be based on a post-market monitoring plan. The post-market monitoring plan shall be part of the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV."
legal_practice_note: High-risk legal-AI providers must include the monitoring plan in technical documentation.

summary: The Commission must adopt guidance, including a template, on the post-market monitoring plan by 2 September 2027, taking utmost account of the Board opinion.
quote: "The Commission, taking utmost account of the opinion of the Board, shall adopt guidance, including a template, on the post-market monitoring plan by 2 September 2027."
legal_practice_note: The guidance will shape documentation expectations for high-risk legal-AI providers.

summary: For Annex I Section A product systems with equivalent sectoral post-market monitoring, providers may integrate the AI Act elements into existing systems and plans.
quote: "providers shall have a choice of integrating, as appropriate, the necessary elements described in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 using the template referred in paragraph 3 into systems and plans already existing under that legislation"
legal_practice_note: This mainly concerns product-regulated high-risk systems rather than legal-practice deployments.

summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market must report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities where the incident occurred.
quote: "Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred."
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI vendors of high-risk systems must report serious incidents in the relevant Member State.

summary: The serious-incident report must be made immediately after causal link or reasonable likelihood is established, and no later than 15 days after awareness.
quote: "not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, becomes aware of the serious incident."
legal_practice_note: This fixes the ordinary reporting deadline for high-risk legal-AI serious incidents.

summary: For a widespread infringement or an Article 3(49)(b) serious incident, the report must be immediate and no later than two days after awareness.
quote: "the report referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall be provided immediately, and not later than two days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer becomes aware of that incident."
legal_practice_note: High-risk legal-AI providers have a shorter two-day deadline for the specified serious incidents.

summary: Where a serious incident involves a death, the report must be immediate after causal relationship is established or suspected, and no later than 10 days after awareness.
quote: "in the event of the death of a person, the report shall be provided immediately after the provider or the deployer has established, or as soon as it suspects, a causal relationship"
legal_practice_note: This special deadline applies to high-risk systems, including any high-risk legal AI linked to death.

summary: Where needed for timely reporting, the provider or applicable deployer may submit an incomplete initial report followed by a complete report.
quote: "the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, may submit an initial report that is incomplete, followed by a complete report."
legal_practice_note: This permits staged reporting for high-risk legal-AI incidents when complete facts are not yet available.

summary: After reporting a serious incident, the provider must investigate without delay, including risk assessment of the incident and corrective action.
quote: "the provider shall, without delay, perform the necessary investigations in relation to the serious incident and the AI system concerned. This shall include a risk assessment of the incident, and corrective action."
legal_practice_note: A high-risk legal-AI provider must investigate reported incidents and take corrective action.

summary: When notified of an Article 3(49)(c) serious incident, the relevant market surveillance authority must inform the fundamental-rights authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1).
quote: "the relevant market surveillance authority shall inform the national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1)."
legal_practice_note: Serious incidents affecting fundamental-rights obligations may reach equality, data-protection or similar authorities relevant to legal disputes.

summary: The Commission must develop dedicated serious-incident reporting guidance by 2 August 2025 and assess it regularly.
quote: "The Commission shall develop dedicated guidance to facilitate compliance with the obligations set out in paragraph 1 of this Article. That guidance shall be issued by 2 August 2025, and shall be assessed regularly."
legal_practice_note: The guidance informs high-risk legal-AI serious-incident reporting practice.

summary: The market surveillance authority must take appropriate Regulation 2019/1020 measures within seven days of receiving a serious-incident notification and follow notification procedures.
quote: "The market surveillance authority shall take appropriate measures, as provided for in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, within seven days from the date it received the notification"
legal_practice_note: This governs regulatory response to serious incidents involving high-risk legal AI.

summary: For Annex III high-risk systems covered by equivalent Union reporting instruments, serious-incident notification is limited to Article 3(49)(c) incidents.
quote: "the notification of serious incidents shall be limited to those referred to in Article 3, point (49)(c)."
legal_practice_note: This may affect high-risk legal-sector systems only if equivalent Union reporting obligations already apply.

summary: For high-risk AI that is, or is a safety component of, covered medical devices, Article 3(49)(c) serious incidents must be notified to the chosen national competent authority.
quote: "shall be made to the national competent authority chosen for that purpose by the Member States where the incident occurred."
legal_practice_note: This is mainly relevant to medical-device AI rather than legal practice.

summary: National competent authorities must immediately notify the Commission of any serious incident, whether or not they have acted on it.
quote: "National competent authorities shall immediately notify the Commission of any serious incident, whether or not they have taken action on it, in accordance with Article 20 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020."
legal_practice_note: This ensures Commission visibility of serious incidents involving high-risk systems, including legal-sector systems.

summary: Regulation 2019/1020 applies to AI systems covered by the AI Act, with references to economic operators and products read as operators and AI systems.
quote: "Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply to AI systems covered by this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: Market-surveillance powers can reach legal-sector AI operators when their systems fall within the Act.

summary: Market surveillance authorities must annually report competition-relevant information, prohibited-practice use and measures taken to the Commission and relevant competition authorities.
quote: "They shall also annually report to the Commission about the use of prohibited practices that occurred during that year and about the measures taken."
legal_practice_note: Reports on prohibited practices can include legal-sector AI uses if discovered during market surveillance.

summary: For high-risk AI related to Annex I Section A products, the sectoral market surveillance authority under that legislation acts as AI Act market surveillance authority.
quote: "the market surveillance authority for the purposes of this Regulation shall be the authority responsible for market surveillance activities designated under those legal acts."
legal_practice_note: This mostly concerns product-regulated AI outside ordinary legal practice.

summary: Articles 79 to 83 procedures do not apply to Annex I Section A product-related AI where equivalent sectoral procedures with the same objective already apply.
quote: "the relevant sectoral procedures shall apply instead."
legal_practice_note: This limits overlap for product-regulated systems and is mostly indirect for legal practice.

summary: Market surveillance authorities may exercise specified Regulation 2019/1020 powers remotely where appropriate to enforce the AI Act effectively.
quote: "market surveillance authorities may exercise the powers referred to in Article 14(4), points (d) and (j), of that Regulation remotely, as appropriate."
legal_practice_note: Remote investigative or enforcement powers may affect legal-AI providers and deployers subject to market surveillance.

summary: For high-risk AI used by financial institutions in direct connection with financial services, the relevant financial supervisory authority acts as market surveillance authority.
quote: "the market surveillance authority for the purposes of this Regulation shall be the relevant national authority responsible for the financial supervision of those institutions"
legal_practice_note: In-house legal teams at financial institutions may deal with financial supervisors as AI Act market surveillance authorities.

summary: A Member State may identify another relevant authority as market surveillance authority in appropriate circumstances if coordination is ensured.
quote: "another relevant authority may be identified by the Member State as market surveillance authority for the purposes of this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: This is institutional allocation of supervisory responsibility.

summary: For specified Annex III law-enforcement, border, justice and democracy systems, Member States must designate data-protection supervisory authorities or similarly conditioned authorities.
quote: "Member States shall designate as market surveillance authorities for the purposes of this Regulation either the competent data protection supervisory authorities"
legal_practice_note: This covers Annex III point 8 administration-of-justice systems and therefore court-facing legal AI.

summary: Market surveillance activities must not affect judicial independence or interfere with judicial authorities when they act in their judicial capacity.
quote: "Market surveillance activities shall in no way affect the independence of judicial authorities, or otherwise interfere with their activities when acting in their judicial capacity."
legal_practice_note: This is directly relevant to courts deploying or overseeing AI in judicial work.

summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor acts as market surveillance authority for Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, except for the CJEU acting judicially.
quote: "the European Data Protection Supervisor shall act as their market surveillance authority, except in relation to the Court of Justice of the European Union acting in its judicial capacity."
legal_practice_note: This may affect EU institutions using legal or adjudicative AI, while preserving the CJEU judicial capacity exception.

summary: Member States must facilitate coordination between AI Act market surveillance authorities and other relevant national or Union-law supervisory authorities.
quote: "Member States shall facilitate coordination between market surveillance authorities designated under this Regulation and other relevant national authorities or bodies"
legal_practice_note: Coordinated supervision may involve justice, data-protection or sectoral bodies relevant to legal-sector AI.

summary: Market surveillance authorities and the Commission may propose joint compliance, investigation, awareness or guidance activities for high-risk AI presenting serious risk in multiple Member States; the AI Office supports coordination.
quote: "Market surveillance authorities and the Commission shall be able to propose joint activities, including joint investigations"
legal_practice_note: Cross-border investigations may affect high-risk legal-AI systems deployed in multiple Member States.

summary: Providers must grant market surveillance authorities full access to documentation and training, validation and testing data sets where relevant and necessary for their tasks.
quote: "the market surveillance authorities shall be granted full access by providers to the documentation as well as the training, validation and testing data sets used for the development of high-risk AI systems"
legal_practice_note: High-risk legal-AI providers may have to provide documentation and datasets to regulators.

summary: Market surveillance authorities may access high-risk AI source code on reasoned request only when source access is necessary and other data, documentation and audit methods are exhausted or insufficient.
quote: "Market surveillance authorities shall be granted access to the source code of the high-risk AI system upon a reasoned request and only when both of the following conditions are fulfilled:"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI providers of high-risk systems may face source-code access requests in narrow circumstances.

summary: Information and documentation obtained by market surveillance authorities under Article 74 must be treated under Article 78 confidentiality obligations.
quote: "Any information or documentation obtained by market surveillance authorities shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78."
legal_practice_note: Confidentiality is important for legal-AI vendors providing sensitive documentation, data or source code.

summary: The AI Office is exclusively competent for supervision and enforcement for AI systems based on general-purpose AI models developed by the same provider or same undertaking, subject to listed exceptions.
quote: "The AI Office shall be exclusively competent for the supervision and enforcement of the obligations under this Regulation in relation to the following AI systems:"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI systems based on an in-house or same-undertaking GPAI model may fall under AI Office supervision unless an exception applies.

summary: The AI Office is exclusively competent for AI systems that constitute or are integrated into designated very large online platforms or very large online search engines.
quote: "AI systems that constitute or that are integrated into a very large online platform or very large online search engine designated in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2022/2065."
legal_practice_note: This mainly affects platform and search-engine AI rather than ordinary legal practice.

summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems supervised by the AI Office must report serious incidents to the AI Office, with Article 73(2) to (9) applying mutatis mutandis; the AI Office must transmit relevant information onward.
quote: "providers of high-risk AI systems subject to the competence of the AI Office pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article shall report any serious incidents to the AI Office."
legal_practice_note: High-risk legal-AI providers under AI Office competence report serious incidents to the AI Office rather than national market surveillance authorities.

summary: Authorities involved in applying the AI Act must cooperate actively with and provide necessary assistance to the AI Office, including for inspections or other enforcement measures.
quote: "The authorities involved in the application of this Regulation shall cooperate actively with the AI Office and provide the AI Office the necessary assistance for the exercise of its powers"
legal_practice_note: National cooperation can affect investigations of legal-AI systems supervised by the AI Office.

summary: When AI Office investigatory or enforcement action in a Member State involves access to a public authority data or AI system, the relevant market surveillance authority must assist.
quote: "the AI Office shall be assisted by the relevant market surveillance authority."
legal_practice_note: This can matter for public-authority or court systems containing legal or justice data.

summary: Before prohibiting, restricting, withdrawing or recalling an AI system on a national market, the AI Office must notify the competent market surveillance authority without undue delay and consult where appropriate.
quote: "the AI Office shall, without undue delay, notify the market surveillance authority competent for that market of its intention to take such a decision."
legal_practice_note: This coordinates AI Office action affecting systems available to legal-sector deployers in national markets.

summary: For Article 75(1) AI systems that are high-risk and require third-party conformity assessment under Article 43, the AI Office is responsible for pre-market assessments and tests, with delegated notified bodies acting for the Commission.
quote: "The AI Office shall be responsible for conformity assessments and tests of AI systems referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article that are classified as high-risk"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI vendors under AI Office competence may face AI Office-led conformity testing before market placement.

summary: If a notified body delegated to perform Article 75(1e) tests or assessments does not perform adequately, the Commission may withdraw the delegation immediately.
quote: "the Commission may withdraw the delegation with immediate effect."
legal_practice_note: This is notified-body oversight with indirect effects on high-risk legal-AI conformity assessment capacity.

summary: Where market surveillance authorities have sufficient reason to consider directly deployable general-purpose AI systems usable for a high-risk purpose non-compliant, they must cooperate with the AI Office on compliance evaluations and inform the Board and other authorities.
quote: "they shall cooperate with the AI Office to carry out compliance evaluations, and shall inform the Board and other market surveillance authorities accordingly."
legal_practice_note: General-purpose AI systems used directly for high-risk legal or justice purposes may trigger joint evaluations.

summary: A market surveillance authority with well-founded and sufficient reasons to suspect infringement by an Article 75(1) provider or deployer may request AI Office assessment through the single point of contact.
quote: "it may request, through the relevant single point of contact designated in accordance with Article 70(2), the AI Office to assess the matter"
legal_practice_note: National authorities can route suspected infringements involving AI Office-supervised legal-AI systems to the AI Office.

summary: Where a market surveillance authority cannot conclude a high-risk AI investigation because it lacks information on the GPAI model, it may request AI Office enforcement of access; the AI Office must supply relevant information within 30 days.
quote: "the AI Office shall supply to the applicant authority without delay, and in any event within 30 days, any information that the AI Office considers to be relevant"
legal_practice_note: This supports investigations of high-risk legal AI that depends on general-purpose models.

summary: For Article 75(1) supervision and enforcement, the AI Office has all market-surveillance powers in the AI Act section and Regulation 2019/1020 and may reclaim supervision and enforcement costs for non-compliance.
quote: "the AI Office shall have all the powers of a market surveillance authority provided for in this Section and in Article 14(4) and Article 16(3) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020."
legal_practice_note: Operators of legal-AI systems under AI Office competence can face market-surveillance powers and cost recovery.

summary: Where the AI Office has reasonable grounds to suspect non-compliance by an Article 75(1) provider or deployer, it may start an investigation and must notify the operator.
quote: "it may adopt a decision to start an investigation into that non-compliance in accordance with Article 14(4), point (f) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020."
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI providers or deployers under AI Office competence may become subject to AI Office investigations.

summary: The AI Office may exercise its powers on its own initiative or following an Article 85 complaint, even before formally starting an investigation.
quote: "The AI Office may exercise the powers referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article on its own initiative or following a complaint received pursuant to Article 85 of this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Complaints may trigger AI Office powers against supervised legal-AI systems before a formal investigation starts.

summary: The AI Office may use specified information-gathering and access powers by simple request or by formal decision.
quote: "The AI Office may exercise the powers listed in Article 14(4), points (a), (b) and (c) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Article 74(12) and (13) of this Regulation by simple request or by decision."
legal_practice_note: This defines how the AI Office can request information or access from supervised legal-AI operators.

summary: The AI Office may conduct necessary remote or on-site inspections for its section tasks and must inform the provider of the subject, purpose, possible fines, review right and notify the relevant market surveillance authority beforehand.
quote: "the AI Office may conduct all necessary remote or on-site inspections pursuant to the powers laid down in Article 14(4), points (d) and (e) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020"
legal_practice_note: AI Office inspections may affect legal-AI providers under Article 75(1).

summary: At the AI Office request, a Member State market surveillance authority may carry out investigations, inspections or other fact-finding measures in its territory on behalf of the AI Office.
quote: "the competent market surveillance authority of a Member State may in its own territory carry out any investigation, inspection or other fact-finding measure on behalf and for the account of the AI Office"
legal_practice_note: National authorities may assist AI Office investigations of legal-AI systems located in their territory.

summary: In Article 75(1) competences, the AI Office may order operators to provide access and explanations for AI systems and to retain data and documents needed to assess implementation and compliance.
quote: "order operators to provide access to, and explanations relating to, their AI systems;"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI operators under AI Office competence may receive access, explanation and retention orders.

summary: The AI Office may appoint independent experts, auditors, investigative teams and Member State experts to support monitoring and enforcement expertise, and share resulting information with relevant national authorities.
quote: "the AI Office may appoint independent external experts and auditors, as well as experts, investigative teams and auditors from the Member State’s competent authorities"
legal_practice_note: This is institutional support for AI Office supervision and may indirectly affect supervised legal-AI systems.

summary: Information collected under Article 75a may be used only for the purposes of the AI Act.
quote: "Information collected pursuant to this Article shall be used only for the purpose of this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: This limits use of information collected from supervised legal-AI providers or deployers.

summary: During Article 75a(2) proceedings, if the operator offers commitments to ensure compliance, the AI Office may make them binding and declare no further grounds for action.
quote: "the AI Office may, by decision, make those commitments binding on the operator concerned and declare that there are no further grounds for action."
legal_practice_note: Operators of supervised legal-AI systems may resolve AI Office proceedings through binding commitments.

summary: The AI Office may reopen commitment proceedings where there has been a material change in the facts on which its decision was based.
quote: "there has been a material change in any of the facts on which the decision was based;"
legal_practice_note: AI Office commitments involving legal-AI operators can be reopened if the factual basis materially changes.

summary: The AI Office may reopen proceedings where the operator acts contrary to commitments that were made binding.
quote: "the operator acts contrary to its commitments;"
legal_practice_note: A supervised legal-AI operator that breaches commitments can face reopened AI Office proceedings.

summary: The AI Office may reopen proceedings where its commitment decision was based on incomplete, incorrect or misleading information from the operator.
quote: "the decision was based on incomplete, incorrect or misleading information provided by the operator concerned."
legal_practice_note: Incomplete or misleading information from a legal-AI operator can reopen AI Office proceedings.

summary: Where offered commitments cannot ensure effective compliance with the AI Act, the AI Office must reject them in a reasoned decision when concluding proceedings.
quote: "it shall reject those commitments in a reasoned decision when concluding the proceedings."
legal_practice_note: AI Office proceedings against supervised legal-AI operators need not end through inadequate commitments.

summary: If the AI Office finds that an Article 75(1) operator does not comply with the Act or binding commitments, it must adopt a decision establishing non-compliance.
quote: "it shall adopt a decision establishing such non-compliance."
legal_practice_note: Supervised legal-AI operators can receive AI Office non-compliance decisions.

summary: Before adopting a non-compliance decision, the AI Office must communicate preliminary findings and explain measures it is considering or considers the operator should take.
quote: "the AI Office shall communicate its preliminary findings to the operator concerned."
legal_practice_note: This gives supervised legal-AI operators notice of the AI Office case and contemplated measures.

summary: In a non-compliance decision, the AI Office may order necessary measures within a specified reasonable period and require information on intended and implemented compliance measures.
quote: "the AI Office shall, where relevant, order the operator concerned to take the necessary measures to ensure compliance with the relevant provisions of this Regulation within a reasonable period specified therein"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI operators under AI Office competence may be ordered to remedy non-compliance and report implementation.

summary: Before requesting any measure, the AI Office may engage in structured dialogue with the operator, during which the operator may propose Article 75b commitments.
quote: "the AI Office may engage in a structured dialogue with the operator of the AI system in question."
legal_practice_note: Structured dialogue can shape commitments or measures for supervised legal-AI systems.

summary: An AI Office non-compliance decision may be accompanied by penalties under Article 99(3) to (7), applied mutatis mutandis to AI Office supervision and enforcement.
quote: "may be accompanied by the imposition of penalties in accordance with Article 99(3) to (7), which provisions shall apply mutatis mutandis to the AI Office"
legal_practice_note: Supervised legal-AI operators can face AI Office-imposed penalties by reference to Article 99 tiers.

summary: The AI Office may impose periodic penalty payments to compel Article 75(1) operators to submit to investigations or inspections, comply with information requests, give correct explanations, carry out corrective actions, comply with commitments or comply with non-compliance decisions.
quote: "The AI Office may adopt a decision imposing periodic penalty payments to compel the operators subject to its competence pursuant to Article 75(1)"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI operators under AI Office competence may face recurring penalties to compel cooperation or compliance.

summary: The Court of Justice has unlimited jurisdiction to review AI Office decisions fixing fines or periodic penalty payments and may cancel, reduce or increase them.
quote: "It may cancel, reduce or increase the fine or periodic penalty payment imposed."
legal_practice_note: This judicial review safeguard can matter to supervised legal-AI operators fined by the AI Office.
cross_references: Court of Justice of the European Union

summary: Funds collected from Article 75c fines or periodic penalty payments contribute to the general budget of the Union.
quote: "Funds collected through the imposition of fines or periodic penalty payments pursuant to this Article shall contribute to the general budget of the Union."
legal_practice_note: This budget rule has no direct legal-practice compliance effect.

summary: AI Office powers under Article 75c are subject to a five-year limitation period running from the infringement, or from cessation for continuing or repeated infringements.
quote: "The powers conferred on the AI Office by this Article shall be subject to a limitation period of five years."
legal_practice_note: This limits the timing of AI Office enforcement against supervised legal-AI operators.

summary: Where the AI Office determines there are no grounds for a non-compliance decision, it must close the proceeding by immediately effective decision.
quote: "Where the AI Office determines that there are no grounds to adopt a decision of non-compliance, it shall close the proceeding by a decision."
legal_practice_note: This ends AI Office proceedings where allegations against a supervised legal-AI operator are not sustained.

summary: Article 18 of Regulation 2019/1020 procedural safeguards apply mutatis mutandis to operators under AI Office competence, without prejudice to more specific AI Act rights.
quote: "Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to operators subject to the AI Office’s competence pursuant to Article 75(1) of this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI operators under AI Office competence receive procedural safeguards.

summary: Operators under Article 75(1) have rights of defence and access to the AI Office file through negotiated disclosure, subject to protection of business secrets and confidential information.
quote: "The rights of defence and of access to the file of operators falling within the scope of Article 75(1) shall be fully respected in proceedings."
legal_practice_note: This protects supervised legal-AI operators in AI Office proceedings.

summary: If parties disagree on negotiated disclosure terms for file access, the AI Office may adopt decisions setting out those terms.
quote: "The AI Office shall have the power to adopt decisions setting out such terms of disclosure in the case of disagreement between the parties."
legal_practice_note: Disclosure decisions may shape access to confidential material in legal-AI enforcement proceedings.

summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts on practical arrangements for file access and negotiated disclosure under Article 75d(2).
quote: "The Commission may adopt implementing acts concerning the practical arrangements for access to the file and the negotiated disclosure of information provided for in paragraph 2."
legal_practice_note: Procedural implementing acts indirectly affect supervised legal-AI operators in AI Office cases.

summary: The AI Office must publish Article 75b and 75c decisions, stating party names and main content including penalties, while respecting confidential information interests.
quote: "The AI Office shall publish the decisions it adopts pursuant to Articles 75b and 75c."
legal_practice_note: Publication can expose enforcement outcomes involving supervised legal-AI operators.

summary: National authorities or bodies supervising Union fundamental-rights obligations have power to request and access necessary AI Act information or documentation from the relevant market surveillance authority in accessible, machine-readable electronic form.
quote: "shall have the power to request and access any information or documentation created or maintained from the relevant market surveillance authority pursuant to this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Fundamental-rights authorities may obtain information about high-risk legal or justice AI affecting discrimination or other rights.

summary: Subject to Article 77 conditions, the market surveillance authority must grant those public authorities or bodies access, including by requesting information from providers or deployers where necessary and without undue delay.
quote: "the market surveillance authority shall grant the relevant public authority or body referred to in paragraph 1 access to such information or documentation"
legal_practice_note: This can require regulator-to-regulator access to information about legal-AI providers or deployers.

summary: Market surveillance authorities and fundamental-rights authorities must cooperate closely, provide mutual assistance and exchange necessary information to ensure coherent application and streamlined procedures.
quote: "Market surveillance authorities and public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 shall cooperate closely and provide each other with the mutual assistance necessary"
legal_practice_note: This supports coordinated handling of legal-AI systems that raise fundamental-rights issues.

summary: Each Member State must identify Article 77(1) public authorities or bodies, publish the list, notify the Commission and other Member States, and keep the list updated.
quote: "each Member State shall identify the public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 and make a list of them publicly available."
legal_practice_note: This identifies authorities that may be involved in legal-AI fundamental-rights supervision.

summary: Where documentation is insufficient to determine whether Union fundamental-rights obligations were infringed, the public authority or body may request technical testing and the market surveillance authority must organise it with close involvement of the requester.
quote: "the public authority or body referred to in paragraph 1 may make a reasoned request to the market surveillance authority, to organise testing of the high-risk AI system through technical means."
legal_practice_note: High-risk legal or justice AI can be technically tested where rights authorities cannot assess infringements from documentation alone.

summary: Information or documentation obtained by national fundamental-rights authorities or bodies under Article 77 must be treated under Article 78 confidentiality obligations.
quote: "Any information or documentation obtained by the national public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article pursuant to this Article shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78."
legal_practice_note: Confidentiality protects legal-AI providers and deployers when information reaches rights authorities.

summary: The Commission, market surveillance authorities, notified bodies and others applying the Act must respect confidentiality of information and data obtained in their tasks and activities.
quote: "shall, in accordance with Union or national law, respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks and activities"
legal_practice_note: Confidentiality is important for legal-AI vendors and deployers sharing sensitive documentation, data or source code.

summary: Confidentiality must protect intellectual property, trade secrets, effective enforcement, public and national security, criminal or administrative proceedings, and classified information.
quote: "the intellectual property rights and confidential business information or trade secrets of a natural or legal person, including source code"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI source code, trade secrets and sensitive enforcement information receive express confidentiality protection.

summary: Authorities applying the Act must request only strictly necessary data, protect obtained information with adequate and effective cybersecurity measures, and delete data when no longer needed.
quote: "shall request only data that is strictly necessary for the assessment of the risk posed by AI systems and for the exercise of their powers"
legal_practice_note: This limits and secures regulatory data collection from legal-AI providers and deployers.

summary: Confidential information exchanged among national competent authorities or with the Commission must not be disclosed without prior consultation of the originating authority and deployer in specified law-enforcement, border, immigration or asylum uses where disclosure would jeopardise security.
quote: "shall not be disclosed without prior consultation of the originating national competent authority and the deployer"
legal_practice_note: This safeguards sensitive public-authority deployments and may affect justice-related AI where security interests arise.

summary: The Commission and Member States may exchange necessary confidential information with third-country regulatory authorities under international or trade agreements and confidentiality arrangements with adequate protection.
quote: "The Commission and Member States may exchange, where necessary and in accordance with relevant provisions of international and trade agreements, confidential information with regulatory authorities of third countries"
legal_practice_note: This is cross-border regulatory cooperation and is usually indirect for legal practice.

summary: For market-surveillance procedure, AI systems presenting health, safety or fundamental-rights risks are treated as products presenting a risk under Regulation 2019/1020.
quote: "AI systems presenting a risk shall be understood as a ‘product presenting a risk’ as defined in Article 3, point 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020"
legal_practice_note: This frames regulatory action for risky legal-AI systems that affect rights, health or safety.

summary: Where a Member State market surveillance authority has sufficient reason to consider an AI system risky, it must evaluate compliance, pay particular attention to vulnerable groups, cooperate with Article 77 bodies when fundamental-rights risks appear, and operators must cooperate as necessary.
quote: "it shall carry out an evaluation of the AI system concerned in respect of its compliance with all the requirements and obligations laid down in this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: Risk evaluations can cover legal-AI systems affecting clients, litigants, employees or vulnerable groups.

summary: If non-compliance is not restricted to its territory, the market surveillance authority must inform the Commission and other Member States without undue delay of evaluation results and required operator actions.
quote: "it shall inform the Commission and the other Member States without undue delay of the results of the evaluation and of the actions which it has required the operator to take."
legal_practice_note: Cross-border legal-AI deployments may prompt EU-wide notices of required operator actions.

summary: The operator must ensure all appropriate corrective action is taken for all AI systems concerned that it has made available on the Union market.
quote: "The operator shall ensure that all appropriate corrective action is taken in respect of all the AI systems concerned that it has made available on the Union market."
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI providers or other operators must remedy risky systems they made available in the Union.

summary: If the AI system operator fails to take adequate corrective action in time, the market surveillance authority must take provisional measures to prohibit, restrict, withdraw or recall the AI system and notify the Commission and other Member States.
quote: "the market surveillance authority shall take all appropriate provisional measures to prohibit or restrict the AI system’s being made available on its national market or put into service"
legal_practice_note: Risky legal-AI systems can be restricted, withdrawn or recalled if operators do not correct them.

summary: The provisional-measure notification must include identifying, origin, supply-chain, non-compliance, risk, measure and operator-argument details and state whether the issue concerns Article 5, Chapter III Section 2, standards or Article 50.
quote: "The notification referred to in paragraph 5 shall include all available details"
legal_practice_note: This structures regulator notices that may concern prohibited, high-risk or transparency obligations in legal-sector AI.

summary: Other Member State market surveillance authorities must inform the Commission and Member States without undue delay of measures, additional information or objections concerning the notified non-compliance.
quote: "shall, without undue delay, inform the Commission and the other Member States of any measures adopted and of any additional information at their disposal relating to the non-compliance"
legal_practice_note: This coordinates national responses to risky legal-AI systems across Member States.

summary: If no objection is raised within three months, or within 30 days for Article 5 non-compliance, another authority provisional measure is deemed justified; market surveillance authorities must then ensure appropriate restrictive measures without undue delay.
quote: "that measure shall be deemed justified."
legal_practice_note: Uncontested restrictions can become justified and lead to wider restrictive measures affecting legal-AI systems.

summary: The Commission must develop guidelines on practical implementation of the Regulation, including high-risk requirements and obligations, prohibited practices, substantial modification, transparency duties, legal relationships and the AI-system definition.
quote: "The Commission shall develop guidelines on the practical implementation of this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Guidance on prohibited practices, high-risk duties, transparency and AI-system definition is directly relevant to legal-AI providers and deployers.

summary: The Commission must publish by 1 August 2027 guidelines on implementing Articles 8(2), 9(10) and 17(3) consistently with Annex I Section A Union harmonisation legislation while avoiding duplication and additional burdens.
quote: "such guidelines shall be published by 1 August 2027."
legal_practice_note: This guidance mainly affects high-risk product AI, with indirect relevance for legal-AI vendors in regulated products.

summary: The Commission must update previously adopted guidelines when necessary, whether at Member State or AI Office request or on its own initiative.
quote: "the Commission shall update guidelines previously adopted when deemed necessary."
legal_practice_note: Updated guidance can affect legal-sector interpretations of AI Act obligations.

summary: The Commission power to adopt delegated acts is conferred subject to the conditions set out in Article 97.
quote: "The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article."
legal_practice_note: Delegated-act mechanics shape the Act but do not directly impose legal-practice obligations.

summary: The delegated-act powers for listed AI Act provisions are conferred on the Commission for five years from 1 August 2024.
quote: "shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 1 August 2024."
legal_practice_note: This includes delegated powers that can affect high-risk and GPAI obligations relevant to legal-AI vendors.

summary: The delegated-act powers referred to in Articles 2(13) and 30(2) are conferred on the Commission for five years from 27 July 2026.
quote: "The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 2(13) and Article 30(2) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 27 July 2026."
transitional_note: New delegation period runs from 27 July 2026.
legal_practice_note: This Omnibus-added delegation includes Annex XIV-related notification scope for notified-body designation.

summary: The Commission must report on delegated powers before each five-year period ends, and the delegation is tacitly extended unless Parliament or Council opposes in time.
quote: "The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period."
legal_practice_note: This is legislative oversight of delegated powers with indirect impact on AI Act rules.

summary: The European Parliament or Council may revoke listed delegations at any time; revocation ends the specified delegation prospectively without affecting delegated acts already in force.
quote: "may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or by the Council."
legal_practice_note: Revocation affects future delegated amendments, including rules relevant to legal-AI compliance.

summary: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission must consult Member State experts, notify Parliament and Council after adoption, and the act enters into force only absent objection within the Article 97 period.
quote: "Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State"
legal_practice_note: Procedural controls on delegated acts indirectly affect future legal-AI compliance rules.

summary: Member States must lay down rules on penalties and other enforcement measures for any AI Act infringement by operators and ensure effective implementation, with effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties and attention to SMEs and SMCs.
quote: "Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties and other enforcement measures, which may also include administrative fines, warnings and non-monetary measures, applicable to any infringement of this Regulation by operators"
legal_practice_note: National penalty rules determine exposure for legal-AI providers, deployers and other operators.

summary: Member States must notify the Commission of penalty and enforcement-measure rules by the date of entry into application and notify subsequent amendments without delay.
quote: "The Member States shall, without delay and at the latest by the date of entry into application, notify the Commission of the rules on penalties and of other enforcement measures"
legal_practice_note: This supports transparency around national penalty regimes affecting legal-sector AI operators.

summary: Non-compliance with Article 5 prohibited AI practices is subject to administrative fines up to EUR 35,000,000 or, for undertakings, 7% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.
quote: "administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher."
legal_practice_note: Article 5 prohibited-practice penalties can apply to legal-AI providers or deployers engaging in prohibited practices.

summary: Non-compliance with specified operator, notified-body and transparency provisions is subject to fines up to EUR 15,000,000 or, for undertakings, 3% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.
quote: "administrative fines of up to EUR 15 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 3 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher:"
legal_practice_note: This is the main fine tier for high-risk provider/deployer duties and transparency duties relevant to legal-AI vendors and users.

summary: Supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in response to a request is subject to fines up to EUR 7,500,000 or 1% of worldwide turnover, whichever is higher.
quote: "administrative fines of up to EUR 7 500 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 1 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher."
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI operators responding to regulators or notified bodies must avoid incorrect, incomplete or misleading information.

summary: For SMEs, including start-ups, each Article 99 fine is capped at the lower of the percentage or amount referred to in paragraphs 3, 4 and 5.
quote: "In the case of SMEs, including start-ups, each fine referred to in this Article shall be up to the percentages or amount referred to in paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, whichever thereof is lower."
legal_practice_note: Small legal-tech vendors may benefit from the SME lower-of cap across Article 99 fine tiers.

summary: For SMCs, each fine under Article 99(4) and (5) is capped at the lower of the percentage or amount stated in those paragraphs.
quote: "In the case of SMCs, each fine referred to in paragraphs 4 and 5 shall be up to the percentages or amount referred therein, whichever is lower."
legal_practice_note: Small mid-cap legal-tech or legal-service operators receive lower-of treatment for the 3%/EUR 15 million and 1%/EUR 7.5 million tiers.

summary: Authorities deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and its amount must consider all relevant circumstances, including gravity, duplicate penalties, size, aggravating or mitigating factors, cooperation, responsibility, notification, intent and mitigation.
quote: "all relevant circumstances of the specific situation shall be taken into account"
legal_practice_note: These factors shape penalty exposure for legal-AI providers, deployers and other operators.

summary: Each Member State must set rules on the extent to which administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies established in that Member State.
quote: "Each Member State shall lay down rules on to what extent administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies established in that Member State."
legal_practice_note: Courts and public legal bodies deploying AI may face national rules on public-authority fines.

summary: Depending on national legal systems, administrative-fine rules may be applied by competent national courts or other bodies, with equivalent effect.
quote: "the rules on administrative fines may be applied in such a manner that the fines are imposed by competent national courts or by other bodies"
legal_practice_note: National courts may be involved in imposing AI Act administrative fines, depending on Member State systems.

summary: Exercise of Article 99 powers must be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards under Union and national law, including effective judicial remedies and due process.
quote: "The exercise of powers under this Article shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and national law, including effective judicial remedies and due process."
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI operators subject to penalties have procedural-safeguard and remedy protections.

summary: Member States must annually report to the Commission on Article 99 administrative fines issued during the year and related litigation or judicial proceedings.
quote: "Member States shall, on an annual basis, report to the Commission about the administrative fines they have issued during that year"
legal_practice_note: This can reveal enforcement involving legal-AI operators and related proceedings.

summary: The Commission may fine GPAI model providers up to 3% of annual total worldwide turnover or EUR 15,000,000, whichever is higher, for intentional or negligent listed infringements.
quote: "fines not exceeding 3 % of their annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000 , whichever is higher."
applies_from_basis: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI vendors that also provide GPAI models may be exposed to this Commission fine tier.
applies_from_basis_as_enacted: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))

summary: Fine triggers include infringing relevant AI Act provisions, failing to comply with Article 91 document or information requests, failing Article 93 measures, or failing to provide model access for Article 92 evaluation.
quote: "when the Commission finds that the provider intentionally or negligently:"
applies_from_basis: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))
legal_practice_note: This identifies the conduct by GPAI providers that can trigger fines, including model-access and information failures.
applies_from_basis_as_enacted: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))

summary: Before adopting an Article 101 fine decision, the Commission must communicate preliminary findings to the GPAI model provider and give it an opportunity to be heard.
quote: "the Commission shall communicate its preliminary findings to the provider of the general-purpose AI model and give it an opportunity to be heard."
applies_from_basis: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))
legal_practice_note: GPAI providers connected to legal-AI services receive hearing rights before Commission fines.
applies_from_basis_as_enacted: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))

summary: Fines imposed under Article 101 must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.
quote: "Fines imposed in accordance with this Article shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive."
applies_from_basis: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))
legal_practice_note: This governs Commission fine calibration for GPAI providers, including legal-AI model providers.
applies_from_basis_as_enacted: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))

summary: Information on Article 101 fines must also be communicated to the AI Board as appropriate.
quote: "Information on fines imposed under this Article shall also be communicated to the Board as appropriate."
applies_from_basis: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))
legal_practice_note: This is governance reporting about GPAI fines and has indirect legal-practice relevance.
applies_from_basis_as_enacted: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))

summary: The Court of Justice may review Commission fine decisions with unlimited jurisdiction, and the Commission must adopt implementing acts on detailed arrangements and procedural safeguards.
quote: "It may cancel, reduce or increase the fine imposed."
applies_from_basis: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))
legal_practice_note: GPAI providers serving legal markets can seek judicial review and benefit from procedural safeguards.
cross_references: Court of Justice of the European Union
applies_from_basis_as_enacted: Art. 113 second subparagraph (Art. 101 excepted from Art. 113(b))

summary: Article 108 amends Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 Article 17 so that, when adopting implementing acts concerning AI safety components, the Chapter III Section 2 AI Act requirements are taken into account.
quote: "when adopting implementing acts pursuant to paragraph 1 concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components"
legal_practice_note: Aviation safety-component amendments have no direct legal-practice relevance.

summary: Article 108 amends Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 Article 19 so that, when adopting delegated acts concerning AI safety components, the Chapter III Section 2 AI Act requirements are taken into account.
quote: "When adopting delegated acts pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2 concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components"
legal_practice_note: Aviation safety-component amendments have no direct legal-practice relevance.

summary: Article 108 amends Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 Article 43 so that, when adopting implementing acts concerning AI safety components, the Chapter III Section 2 AI Act requirements are taken into account.
quote: "When adopting implementing acts pursuant to paragraph 1 concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components"
legal_practice_note: Aviation safety-component amendments have no direct legal-practice relevance.

summary: Article 108 amends Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 Article 47 so that, when adopting delegated acts concerning AI safety components, the Chapter III Section 2 AI Act requirements are taken into account.
quote: "When adopting delegated acts pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2 concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components"
legal_practice_note: Aviation safety-component amendments have no direct legal-practice relevance.

summary: Article 108 amends Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 Article 57 so that, when adopting implementing acts concerning AI safety components, the Chapter III Section 2 AI Act requirements are taken into account.
quote: "When adopting those implementing acts concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components"
legal_practice_note: Aviation safety-component amendments have no direct legal-practice relevance.

summary: Article 108 amends Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 Article 58 so that, when adopting delegated acts concerning AI safety components, the Chapter III Section 2 AI Act requirements are taken into account.
quote: "When adopting delegated acts pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2 concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components"
legal_practice_note: Aviation safety-component amendments have no direct legal-practice relevance.

summary: Article 110 adds the AI Act to Annex I of Directive 2020/1828, bringing it within the representative-actions framework listed in that Directive.
quote: "In Annex I to Directive (EU) 2020/1828 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 3 ), the following point is added:"
legal_practice_note: Representative actions can matter to legal practice through collective redress linked to AI Act infringements.

summary: AI components of Annex X large-scale IT systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 must be brought into AI Act compliance by 31 December 2030.
quote: "AI systems which are components of the large-scale IT systems established by the legal acts listed in Annex X that have been placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 shall be brought into compliance"
transitional_note: Compliance deadline for covered large-scale IT AI components: 31 December 2030.
legal_practice_note: Large-scale justice and security IT systems may involve public-sector legal contexts.

summary: For other high-risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service before the Chapter III application date, the Regulation applies only if those systems are subject to significant design changes from that date.
quote: "this Regulation shall apply to operators of high-risk AI systems, other than the systems referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, that have been placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III"
transitional_note: Legacy high-risk systems are covered only upon significant design changes from the Chapter III application date, except for the public-authority compliance deadline.
legal_practice_note: Legacy high-risk legal-AI systems may be covered only upon significant design changes, subject to the public-authority rule.

summary: Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended for use by public authorities must take necessary steps to comply with AI Act requirements and obligations by 2 August 2030.
quote: "the providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities shall take the necessary steps to comply with the requirements and obligations laid down in this Regulation by 2 August 2030."
transitional_note: Public-authority high-risk systems compliance deadline: 2 August 2030.
legal_practice_note: Courts and other public legal bodies using high-risk AI receive the 2 August 2030 legacy-system compliance deadline.

summary: Providers of GPAI models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 must take necessary steps to comply with AI Act obligations by 2 August 2027.
quote: "Providers of general-purpose AI models that have been placed on the market before 2 August 2025 shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with the obligations laid down in this Regulation by 2 August 2027."
transitional_note: Legacy GPAI model compliance deadline: 2 August 2027.
legal_practice_note: GPAI model providers serving legal-AI markets may rely on this legacy compliance timetable.

summary: Providers of AI systems, including GPAI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content placed on the market before 2 August 2026 must comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026.
quote: "Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, that have been placed on the market before 2 August 2026 shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026."
transitional_note: Synthetic-content legacy systems compliance deadline: 2 December 2026.
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI systems generating synthetic legal or client-facing text, audio, images or video may need Article 50(2) compliance by the transitional deadline.

summary: The AI Act enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
quote: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union."
legal_practice_note: This sets the legal entry-into-force date.

summary: Unless a specific amended Article 113 exception applies, the AI Act applies from 2 August 2026.
quote: "It shall apply from 2 August 2026. However:"
legal_practice_note: This is the default application date for most legal-sector AI obligations.

summary: Chapters I and II apply from 2 February 2025, except the newly specified Article 5(1) points and Article 5(1a) and (1b) later date.
quote: "Chapters I and II shall apply from 2 February 2025"
legal_practice_note: This brings Article 5 prohibited-practice rules into early application for legal-sector AI, except the new Omnibus items.

summary: Article 5(1) first-subparagraph points (ba) and (bb), and Article 5(1a) and (1b), apply from 2 December 2026 under amended Article 113(a).
quote: "Article 5(1), first subparagraph, points (ba) and (bb), and Article 5(1a) and (1b) which shall apply from 2 December 2026;"
legal_practice_note: These newly staged prohibited-practice provisions may affect legal-sector AI from 2 December 2026.

summary: Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII, Chapter XII and Article 78 apply from 2 August 2025, except Article 101.
quote: "Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101;"
legal_practice_note: Penalties, confidentiality and GPAI governance timelines begin early, while Article 101 remains on the default date.

summary: Chapter III Sections 1 to 3, except Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027 for AI systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(2) and Annex III.
quote: "2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III;"
legal_practice_note: This sets the deferred date for Annex III legal and justice high-risk AI.

summary: Chapter III Sections 1 to 3, except Article 6(5), apply from 2 August 2028 for AI systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(1) and Annex I.
quote: "2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I;"
legal_practice_note: This later date mainly concerns product-safety high-risk systems rather than Annex III legal AI.

summary: Articles 102 to 110 apply from 27 July 2026 under amended Article 113(d).
quote: "Articles 102 to 110 shall apply from 27 July 2026."
legal_practice_note: This accelerates amendments to other acts and related provisions, including representative actions relevance.

summary: Annex XIV explains that only conformity assessment bodies designated under the AI Act may carry out high-risk AI conformity assessments, and only for activities related to the relevant AI-system types.
quote: "Only conformity assessment bodies that have been designated in accordance with this Regulation may carry out conformity assessments"
applies_from_basis: Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 in-force date; Annex XIV inserted for Art. 30(2)
transitional_note: Annex XIV was inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and is treated as applying from that Regulation’s 27 July 2026 in-force date.
legal_practice_note: This is notified-body infrastructure that indirectly affects high-risk legal-AI providers needing conformity assessment.

summary: Annex XIV states that its list of codes, categories and corresponding AI-system types sets the scope of notified-body designation under Article 30.
quote: "The list of codes, categories, and corresponding types of AI systems sets the scope of the designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30."
applies_from_basis: Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 in-force date; Annex XIV inserted for Art. 30(2)
transitional_note: Annex XIV was inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and is treated as applying from that Regulation’s 27 July 2026 in-force date.
legal_practice_note: Designation scope indirectly affects legal-AI providers seeking a notified body.

summary: Annex XIV includes a notification-designation category for AI systems subject to Annex I.
quote: "AI systems subject to Annex I"
applies_from_basis: Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 in-force date; Annex XIV inserted for Art. 30(2)
transitional_note: Annex XIV was inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and is treated as applying from that Regulation’s 27 July 2026 in-force date.
legal_practice_note: This mostly concerns product-regulated high-risk AI outside ordinary legal practice.

summary: Annex XIV includes a notification-designation category for AI systems subject to Annex III point 1.
quote: "AI systems subject to point 1 of Annex III"
applies_from_basis: Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 in-force date; Annex XIV inserted for Art. 30(2)
transitional_note: Annex XIV was inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and is treated as applying from that Regulation’s 27 July 2026 in-force date.
legal_practice_note: This may affect notified-body scope for biometric high-risk systems used in public or legal environments.

summary: Annex XIV establishes technology-specific codes for symbolic AI and expert systems, machine learning excluding generative AI and GPAI systems, GPAI or generative-AI-based systems, and emerging AI technologies.
quote: "AI technology-specific codes"
applies_from_basis: Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 in-force date; Annex XIV inserted for Art. 30(2)
transitional_note: Annex XIV was inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and is treated as applying from that Regulation’s 27 July 2026 in-force date.
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI vendors may rely on notified bodies designated for relevant AI technologies, including expert systems and GPAI-based systems.

summary: Conformity assessment bodies must use the Annex XIV lists when specifying AI-system types in applications for designation under Article 29.
quote: "Conformity assessment bodies shall use the lists of codes, categories and corresponding types of AI systems set out in this Annex when specifying the types of AI systems in the application for designation referred to in Article 29."
applies_from_basis: Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 in-force date; Annex XIV inserted for Art. 30(2)
transitional_note: Annex XIV was inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and is treated as applying from that Regulation’s 27 July 2026 in-force date.
legal_practice_note: This affects conformity assessment bodies rather than legal practitioners directly.
